================================================================================
SSCP CODEBOOK: FRACTIONALISATION
================================================================================

Part of the Small State Coverage Project (SSCP). See the project-level README
for shared conventions (universe of cases, identifier scheme, missing-data
codes). This file documents what is specific to this extension.


Files:			sscp_fractionalisation.csv
Version:		v1.0
Base dataset extended:	Alesina, A., Devleeschauwer, A., Easterly, W., Kurlat,
    S., & Wacziarg, R. (2003). "Fractionalization." Journal of Economic
    Growth, 8(2), 155-194. (Also circulated as NBER Working Paper No. 9411.)
DOI:			10.7910/DVN/EVCQXC


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT THIS EXTENSION ADDS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This extensions covers an additional 38 polities for ethnic fractionalisation, 18 for linguistic fractionalisation, and 25 for religious fractionalisation. Adds ethnic, language, and religious fractionalisation values for mostly small polities not covered by Alesina et al.'s original index:
  - Ethnic and language: from CIA World Factbook group-share data, plus a
    supplementary source for polities the Factbook itself has no ethnic
    breakdown for (see section 4).
  - Religion: from RCS-Dem 2.0 (2015 cross-section).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. VARIABLES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In sscp_fractionalisation.csv:
 
 Field order: Variable name | Type | Description | Coding/units
 
iso_num          | numeric | see project README | -
country          | string  | polity name | -
scope_status     | string  | Whether the polity is in the SSCP universe | "in_scope" if the polity is in universe_of_cases.csv, otherwise "opportunistic" (no year dimension, so assessed per polity)
gw_num           | numeric | Gleditsch & Ward state number | From universe_of_cases.csv; NA if none
gw_alpha         | string  | Gleditsch & Ward state abbreviation | From universe_of_cases.csv; NA if none
cow_num          | numeric | Correlates of War state number | From universe_of_cases.csv; NA if none
cow_alpha        | string  | Correlates of War state abbreviation | From universe_of_cases.csv; NA if none
ethnic_frac      | numeric | Ethnic fractionalisation: probability two randomly selected individuals from the population belong to different ethnic groups | 0-1; 1 - sum(group share^2)
ethnic_source    | string  | Where ethnic_frac came from | "alesina_2003", "cia", "eb", or "wdm"
language_frac    | numeric | Language fractionalisation, same construction as ethnic_frac applied to linguistic groups | 0-1; 1 - sum(group share^2)
language_source  | string  | Where language_frac came from | "alesina_2003" or "cia"
religion_frac    | numeric | Religious fractionalisation, same Herfindahl construction applied to broad religious-group shares | 0-1; 1 - sum(group share^2), floored at 0
religion_source  | string  | Where religion_frac came from | "alesina_2003" or "rcs_dem_2.0"


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. CONSTRUCTION METHOD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4a. Ethnic and language
 
For each added state, ethnic and language group shares were taken from the
CIA World Factbook's "Ethnic Groups" and "Languages" entries. For states
without any Factbook ethnic breakdown, group shares were instead taken from
sources recorded per-row in ethnic_other.csv's `source` field:
 
  - `eb`  : Encyclopaedia Britannica, Britannica Book of the Year 2014
            (Chicago: Encyclopædia Britannica, Inc., 2014), "Nations of the
            World" statistical tables. Britannica's own tables cite whatever
            census/estimate year was current for each country at time of
            publication, which is why the `date` field varies row to row
            even though all `eb` rows come from the same 2014 edition.
  - `wdm` : World Directory of Minorities and Indigenous Peoples, Minority
            Rights Group International (minorityrights.org).
  - `cia` : current CIA World Factbook.
 

4b. Religion
 
Religious group shares were taken from Brown, D., & James, P. (2019, February). 
Religious characteristics of states dataset project – demographics v. 2.0 (rcs-dem 2.0), 
countries only. https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/7SR4M (2015 cross-section),
using the broad religion categories (Christian, Jewish, Muslim, Zroastrian,
Baha'i, Jain, Sikh, Hindu, Buddhist, East Asian complex, new religious
movements, indigenous, other) plus an "unknown" (UNKPC) category.
 
The East Asian complex category (EACPC) is backfilled where RCS-Dem records
it as missing or zero, using the sum of Shinto (SHNPC), Confucian (CNFPC),
Taoist (TAOPC), and Chinese folk (CHFPC) shares.
 
UNKPC (unknown affiliation) is included in the denominator when computing
each group's share of the population, but is not treated as a religious
group in its own rightl, i.e. it drags total_percent (and therefore every
group's share) down, but never appears as a term in the sum-of-squares.
Where reported affiliations sum to under 100% (mostly countries with large
unaffiliated or folk-religion populations underrepresented in RCS-Dem, n=16
in the 2015 cross-section), this has the effect of normalising shares to
sum to 1 rather than leaving fractionalisation understated.



4c. Common to both
 
All variables use the same Herfindahl-based fractionalisation formula,
following Alesina et al. (2003):
 
    frac = 1 - sum(share_i^2)
 
where share_i is group i's share of the population, summed over all
reported groups for that state - the probability that two individuals
drawn at random from the population belong to different groups.
 
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. KNOWN LIMITATIONS / CAVEATS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Ethnic / language:
- Reported group shares do not always sum to 100% in the underlying sources
  (Factbook entries in particular often omit small/unclassified residual
  categories). States with total reported shares well below 100% will have
  understated fractionalisation values. 
- All values are a single cross-sectional snapshot rather than a time series.
 
Religion:
- religion_frac is a 2015 cross-section (RCS-Dem 2.0).
- Countries with total_flag != "ok" (total_percent outside 95-105% before
  normalisation) in religious_frac.csv (n=16) rely on the UNKPC-inclusive
  normalisation described in section 4b.
- The EACPC backfill (section 4b) is a judgment call about how to treat
  missing/zero East Asian complex data.
 
 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. MISSING DATA
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Follows the SSCP-wide missing data convention (NA). No deviations.
